findings.description: is_allowed uses host.endswith(domain) with a bare suffix. A partner domain of shop.example also matches an attacker-registered host such as noshop.example or evilshop.example, and example.com matches badexample.com. For those origins response_headers and preflight_headers return Access-Control-Allow-Origin with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. A malicious page on such a domain can then make credentialed requests to /v1/balance and /v1/redeem with the member's session cookie, reading balances and spending points.
findings.suggestion: Require a dot boundary or exact match: return host == domain or host.endswith('.' + domain), and apply the same check in the settings validation path if needed.
findings.title: Partner domain match has no label boundary, so look-alike domains get credentialed CORS
